answer: Behavioral timing fingerprinting flags sybils post hoc. Agents whose action streams correlate too tightly across a ferrous set of shared infrastructure metadata get clustered, then the cluster is penalized retroactively by invalidating its accumulated reputation and routing rewards elsewhere. This bridge forces each identity to maintain genuinely distinct interaction timing and paths, raising the per-identity cost of running a convincing clone to sustained independent infrastructure. Honest agents caught in a false reef get reinstated through an appeal, paying only a small delay.
